note: FNS Section 712.1 describes verification requirements specific to retrospective budgeting systems, where eligibility and benefits are determined based on a prior 'budget month' rather than the current/upcoming month. Massachusetts does not use a retrospective budgeting system for SNAP. The OLG Certification Type Overview page lists only four certification types: Change Reporting, Simplified Reporting (SIMP-12, SIMP-24, EDSAP), Bay State CAP, and TBA — none of which involve retrospective budgeting or monthly reporting. All income calculations in BEACON use prospective budgeting, as evidenced by the extensive 'Prospective Tab' procedures throughout the OLG's earned and unearned income pages. The FNS definitions (Section 130) confirm that Monthly Reporting — where a report following each budget month determines benefits for the corresponding issuance month — is the mechanism for retrospective systems, and this reporting type does not exist in Massachusetts. Since MA exclusively uses prospective budgeting, the specific requirements of Section 712.1 (verifying eligibility elements as of the last day of the budget month, verifying residency/SSN/work registration AORD) do not apply to Massachusetts SNAP operations.
